headline.text: Varsinais-Suomi lags national figures in crude shares of curative, life-prolonging and symptomatic treatment and recorded MDT meetings, while its crude share with no treatment record within 12 months is higher.

details.text: In Varsinais-Suomi, the crude curative treatment share is 24.3% (95% CI 22.1–26.6; n=349/1437) versus 27.0% (4009/14873) nationally, and the 95% confidence interval excludes the national value.

In figures digitised from Kuva 16 (precision ±0.5 percentage points), the age-adjusted curative gap holds for men at 22.7% versus 26.7% nationally (95% confidence interval bar hidden inside the dot, half-width < ~3.3 percentage points), whereas women are at 27.4% (95% CI 23.1–31.8) versus 26.9% nationally, where the 95% confidence interval includes the national value.

The county's crude share is 9.7% (95% CI 8.3–11.4; n=140/1437) versus 30.4% (4522/14873) nationally for life-prolonging treatment and 30.8% (95% CI 28.5–33.3; n=443/1437) versus 39.5% (5871/14873) nationally for symptomatic treatment, with the 95% confidence intervals excluding the national values.

The crude share with no treatment record within 12 months is 43.1% (95% CI 40.5–45.6; n=619/1437) versus 27.5% (4089/14873) nationally, and the crude share with an MDT meeting recorded is 1.6% (95% CI 1.1–2.4; n=23/1437) versus 6.0% (893/14873) nationally; the 95% confidence intervals exclude the national values.

headline.text: High crude shares with no treatment record suggest unrecorded care may partly explain low treatment figures, while missing stage data and unmeasured pathway dates limit what public data show.

details.text: Because Varsinais-Suomi's 43.1% crude share with no treatment record within 12 months exceeds the 27.5% national figure and mixes untreated patients with unrecorded care, we infer as a data-quality signal that low crude treatment shares may partly reflect unrecorded treatment, whereas a journal article shows HILMO matches Cancer Registry diagnoses for about 90% of most cancer types.

County treatment shares are crude and not adjusted for age or stage because stage at diagnosis is missing for ~48% of new patients, and the 1.6% crude MDT share reflects recording practice rather than care because HILMO captures specialised care procedures only from direct patient contacts.

In public report data, primary care visits are not included in the report's data, occupational health is not mentioned, symptom onset and referrals are unmeasured, imaging appears only as the diagnostic basis in approximately 20% of cases, and specialist visits (93.6% within 12 months) and treatments lack start dates.

Preliminary, unpublished national figures indicate lung cancer takes 155 days on average from first symptoms to first treatment in Finland (56 days patient delay, 41 days primary care interval, and 58 days in specialist care) versus 107 days in Sweden and 67 days in Denmark, but county waiting times are unknown.

headline.text: The team recommends auditing stage, drug treatment and MDT recording completeness first, reporting access times using THL guidance 21/2016 definitions, and standardising referrals and diagnostic coordination.

details.text: Given the 43.1% crude share with no treatment record, 9.7% crude life-prolonging share and 1.6% crude MDT share, the team recommends publishing county recording completeness for stage, drug treatment and MDT coding as data-quality signals first, as data reporting is currently incomplete and the roadmap plans a quality registry with 90% coverage.

Because the Health Care Act sets no maximum time for a cancer suspicion and national monitoring is lacking, the team recommends reporting access times from referral to treatment start using THL guidance 21/2016 definitions (16 cancers) with handover alerts, as the roadmap plans national pathways by 2026–2028 and Filha's diagnostics recommendation is due before the 2030 mid-term evaluation.

Because referrals follow local instructions and mentor insight notes a weak referral gets lower specialist urgency, the team recommends a standard referral template, a primary-care rule referring persistent symptoms after a normal X-ray to a pulmonologist, and a named diagnostic contact person, while the roadmap plans referral criteria and coordinator guidance by 2026–2028.

rec:1.claim_text: Team recommendation 1: Counties report access times using the THL 21/2016 definitions, with handover alerts. Each wellbeing services county reports lung cancer access times (referral → first specialist visit → diagnosis → treatment start) using the definitions in THL's Hoitoonpääsyn seuranta syövän hoidossa (Ohjaus 21/2016). Until national target times exist, flag stalled handovers.
rec:1.location: §1. Counties report access times using the THL 21/2016 definitions, with handover alerts

rec:2.claim_text: Team recommendation 2: A KYS-style referral template, a persistent-symptoms rule and a named contact. Adopt a standard referral content list and template, modelled on KYS. • Add a rule for primary care: if symptoms persist after a normal X-ray, refer for a pulmonologist assessment. • Name a contact person for the diagnostic phase, from referral to diagnosis.
rec:2.location: §2. A KYS-style referral template, a persistent-symptoms rule and a named contact

rec:3.claim_text: Team recommendation 3: Report recording completeness per county: stage, drug treatment, MDT coding. Publish, per county, how completely stage, drug treatment and MDT meetings are recorded. Read county ‘gaps’ in these fields as data-quality signals first.
